description: Mechanisms aligned to the nine Personal Wellness Blueprint body systems

mechanisms.name: Bile Acid Binding
mechanisms.description: Describes how soluble fibres and related compounds bind bile acids in the gut, increasing their excretion and prompting the liver to draw more cholesterol from the blood to make replacement bile acids.
mechanisms.plainEnglish: Helps remove cholesterol from the body by binding to bile acids in the gut.

mechanisms.name: Supports Healthy Cholesterol Metabolism
mechanisms.description: A broader mechanism covering the range of ways foods and compounds can influence cholesterol synthesis, absorption and clearance to support a healthy overall lipid profile.
mechanisms.plainEnglish: Helps keep cholesterol levels in a healthy range.

mechanisms.name: Supports Healthy Triglyceride Metabolism
mechanisms.description: Covers effects on the synthesis, transport and clearance of triglycerides, the main storage form of dietary fat in the blood.
mechanisms.plainEnglish: Helps keep blood fat (triglyceride) levels in a healthy range.

mechanisms.name: Reduces Cholesterol Absorption
mechanisms.description: Describes compounds, such as plant sterols, that compete with dietary cholesterol for absorption in the small intestine, reducing the amount that enters the bloodstream.
mechanisms.plainEnglish: Reduces how much cholesterol from food gets absorbed into the body.

mechanisms.name: Supports HDL Maintenance
mechanisms.description: Covers effects on high-density lipoprotein (HDL) cholesterol, which transports cholesterol away from tissues to the liver for clearance.
mechanisms.plainEnglish: Helps maintain healthy levels of HDL, often called 'good' cholesterol.

mechanisms.name: Supports LDL Reduction
mechanisms.description: Covers effects that help lower low-density lipoprotein (LDL) cholesterol, the lipoprotein most closely associated with arterial plaque build-up.
mechanisms.plainEnglish: Helps lower LDL, often called 'bad' cholesterol.

mechanisms.name: Supports Lipid Transport
mechanisms.description: Describes effects on the lipoproteins and transport proteins responsible for moving fats and cholesterol through the bloodstream.
mechanisms.plainEnglish: Helps the body move fats and cholesterol around efficiently.

mechanisms.name: Supports Lipid Oxidation
mechanisms.description: Covers the breakdown of fatty acids for energy within cells, particularly relevant to fat utilisation and metabolic efficiency.
mechanisms.plainEnglish: Helps the body burn fat for energy.

mechanisms.name: Supports Healthy Lipoprotein Balance
mechanisms.description: A broader mechanism describing effects on the overall balance between different lipoprotein classes (LDL, HDL, VLDL) that determine cardiovascular risk.
mechanisms.plainEnglish: Helps keep the different types of cholesterol-carrying particles in a healthy balance.

mechanisms.name: Supports Endothelial Function
mechanisms.description: Describes support for the health of the endothelium, the thin layer of cells lining blood vessels that regulates vascular tone, clotting and inflammation.
mechanisms.plainEnglish: Helps keep the inner lining of blood vessels healthy.

mechanisms.name: Supports Nitric Oxide Production
mechanisms.description: Covers compounds that support the body's production of nitric oxide, a signalling molecule that relaxes blood vessels and improves blood flow.
mechanisms.plainEnglish: Helps the body produce nitric oxide, which relaxes blood vessels.

mechanisms.name: Supports Vascular Elasticity
mechanisms.description: Describes effects on the flexibility of blood vessel walls, allowing them to expand and contract normally with each heartbeat.
mechanisms.plainEnglish: Helps keep blood vessels flexible and responsive.

mechanisms.name: Supports Healthy Blood Pressure Regulation
mechanisms.description: Covers the range of mechanisms, including vasodilation and reduced arterial stiffness, through which foods can support normal blood pressure.
mechanisms.plainEnglish: Helps support healthy blood pressure.

mechanisms.name: Supports Microcirculation
mechanisms.description: Describes effects on blood flow through the smallest vessels, capillaries and arterioles, which supply oxygen and nutrients to tissues.
mechanisms.plainEnglish: Helps improve blood flow through the smallest blood vessels.

mechanisms.name: Supports Vascular Repair
mechanisms.description: Covers processes involved in maintaining and repairing blood vessel walls following everyday wear or minor damage.
mechanisms.plainEnglish: Helps the body repair and maintain blood vessel walls.

mechanisms.name: Supports Healthy Platelet Function
mechanisms.description: Describes effects on platelet activity and aggregation, relevant to normal blood clotting and vascular health.
mechanisms.plainEnglish: Helps keep blood platelets functioning normally.

mechanisms.name: Supports Capillary Integrity
mechanisms.description: Covers effects on the strength and permeability of capillary walls, the smallest blood vessels in the body.
mechanisms.plainEnglish: Helps keep the smallest blood vessels strong and less prone to leaking.

mechanisms.name: Supports Healthy Blood Flow
mechanisms.description: A broader mechanism describing the combined vascular effects, including vessel dilation and reduced resistance, that support efficient blood flow throughout the body.
mechanisms.plainEnglish: Helps blood flow more easily around the body.

mechanisms.name: Supports Vascular Resilience
mechanisms.description: Describes the vascular system's overall capacity to withstand and recover from everyday physiological stress, such as blood pressure fluctuations.
mechanisms.plainEnglish: Helps blood vessels stay resilient under everyday stress.

mechanisms.name: Reduces Oxidative Stress
mechanisms.description: A broad mechanism describing the reduction of excess reactive oxygen species that can otherwise damage cells, proteins and DNA.
mechanisms.plainEnglish: Helps reduce harmful oxidative damage in the body.

mechanisms.name: Neutralises Free Radicals
mechanisms.description: Describes direct antioxidant activity, where compounds donate electrons to neutralise unstable free radical molecules before they can damage cells.
mechanisms.plainEnglish: Helps neutralise unstable molecules (free radicals) that can damage cells.

mechanisms.name: Activates Endogenous Antioxidant Pathways
mechanisms.description: Covers compounds that trigger the body's own antioxidant defence systems, such as the Nrf2 pathway, rather than acting as antioxidants directly.
mechanisms.plainEnglish: Helps switch on the body's own natural antioxidant defences.

mechanisms.name: Protects Cellular Membranes
mechanisms.description: Describes protection of the lipid membranes surrounding cells from oxidative damage, helping maintain normal cell structure and function.
mechanisms.plainEnglish: Helps protect the outer membrane of cells from damage.

mechanisms.name: Supports Mitochondrial Resilience
mechanisms.description: Covers effects that help protect mitochondria, the energy-producing structures within cells, from oxidative and metabolic stress.
mechanisms.plainEnglish: Helps protect the energy-producing parts of cells.

mechanisms.name: Reduces DNA Oxidative Damage
mechanisms.description: Describes protection of DNA from oxidative damage caused by reactive oxygen species, supporting normal cellular function and repair.
mechanisms.plainEnglish: Helps protect DNA from oxidative damage.

mechanisms.name: Supports Redox Balance
mechanisms.description: Covers the overall balance between oxidising and reducing (antioxidant) processes within cells, important for normal cellular signalling and function.
mechanisms.plainEnglish: Helps keep the body's oxidative balance in a healthy range.

mechanisms.name: Supports Cellular Repair
mechanisms.description: Describes support for the processes by which cells repair everyday damage and maintain normal function.
mechanisms.plainEnglish: Helps cells repair everyday wear and damage.

mechanisms.name: Protects Proteins from Oxidation
mechanisms.description: Covers protection of proteins from oxidative modification, which can otherwise impair their normal structure and function.
mechanisms.plainEnglish: Helps protect proteins in the body from oxidative damage.

mechanisms.name: Supports Healthy Ageing
mechanisms.description: A broad mechanism describing the cumulative antioxidant and cell-protective effects associated with supporting healthy ageing processes.
mechanisms.plainEnglish: Helps support the body's natural, healthy ageing processes.

mechanisms.name: Feeds Beneficial Gut Bacteria
mechanisms.description: Describes prebiotic effects, where fermentable fibres and related compounds selectively nourish beneficial bacteria in the gut.
mechanisms.plainEnglish: Feeds the beneficial bacteria that live in the gut.

mechanisms.name: Increases Short-Chain Fatty Acid Production
mechanisms.description: Covers the fermentation of fibre by gut bacteria into short-chain fatty acids such as butyrate, which nourish colon cells and support gut health.
mechanisms.plainEnglish: Helps gut bacteria produce beneficial short-chain fatty acids.

mechanisms.name: Supports Gut Barrier Integrity
mechanisms.description: Describes support for the intestinal lining, which controls what passes from the gut into the bloodstream and helps prevent unwanted substances from crossing the gut wall.
mechanisms.plainEnglish: Helps keep the lining of the gut strong and well-sealed.

mechanisms.name: Improves Bowel Regularity
mechanisms.description: Covers effects, particularly from dietary fibre, that add bulk or soften stool and support regular, comfortable bowel movements.
mechanisms.plainEnglish: Helps support regular bowel movements.

mechanisms.name: Supports Digestive Enzyme Activity
mechanisms.description: Describes support for the enzymes involved in breaking down food into absorbable nutrients during digestion.
mechanisms.plainEnglish: Helps the body's digestive enzymes work effectively.

mechanisms.name: Supports Microbiome Diversity
mechanisms.description: Covers effects that support a varied population of beneficial bacterial species within the gut microbiome, associated with better overall gut health.
mechanisms.plainEnglish: Helps support a diverse and healthy population of gut bacteria.

mechanisms.name: Supports Healthy Gut pH
mechanisms.description: Describes effects, often via fermentation by-products, that help maintain the mildly acidic environment of the colon associated with beneficial bacterial growth.
mechanisms.plainEnglish: Helps maintain a healthy acid balance in the gut.

mechanisms.name: Supports Nutrient Absorption
mechanisms.description: Covers effects that support the efficient uptake of vitamins, minerals and other nutrients across the intestinal lining.
mechanisms.plainEnglish: Helps the body absorb nutrients from food effectively.

mechanisms.name: Supports Mucosal Health
mechanisms.description: Describes support for the mucus layer lining the digestive tract, which protects the gut wall and supports a healthy environment for beneficial bacteria.
mechanisms.plainEnglish: Helps keep the protective lining of the gut healthy.

mechanisms.name: Reduces Digestive Discomfort
mechanisms.description: Covers effects associated with reduced bloating, gas or general digestive discomfort, often via improved digestion or gut motility.
mechanisms.plainEnglish: Helps reduce everyday digestive discomfort.

mechanisms.name: Slows Glucose Absorption
mechanisms.description: Describes effects, often from soluble fibre forming a viscous gel, that slow the rate at which glucose from food is absorbed into the bloodstream.
mechanisms.plainEnglish: Slows down how quickly sugar from food enters the bloodstream.

mechanisms.name: Improves Insulin Sensitivity
mechanisms.description: Covers effects that improve how effectively cells respond to insulin, supporting more efficient blood glucose uptake.
mechanisms.plainEnglish: Helps the body respond to insulin more effectively.

mechanisms.name: Reduces Post-Meal Glucose Response
mechanisms.description: Describes a reduction in the rise in blood glucose that follows a meal, often referred to as the postprandial glycaemic response.
mechanisms.plainEnglish: Helps reduce the blood sugar spike after eating.

mechanisms.name: Improves Satiety
mechanisms.description: Covers effects that increase feelings of fullness after eating, often via fibre, protein or fat content slowing gastric emptying.
mechanisms.plainEnglish: Helps you feel fuller for longer after eating.

mechanisms.name: Supports Healthy Energy Regulation
mechanisms.description: Describes broader effects on the steadiness of energy availability throughout the day, linked to stable blood glucose and metabolic function.
mechanisms.plainEnglish: Helps keep energy levels steady throughout the day.

mechanisms.name: Supports Glycaemic Stability
mechanisms.description: Covers the overall smoothing of blood glucose fluctuations across meals and over the course of a day.
mechanisms.plainEnglish: Helps keep blood sugar levels steady.

mechanisms.name: Supports Pancreatic Function
mechanisms.description: Describes support for the pancreas's role in producing insulin and other hormones involved in blood glucose regulation.
mechanisms.plainEnglish: Helps support healthy pancreas function.

mechanisms.name: Supports Glucose Uptake
mechanisms.description: Covers effects that support the movement of glucose from the bloodstream into cells, where it can be used for energy.
mechanisms.plainEnglish: Helps cells take up glucose from the blood for energy.

mechanisms.name: Supports Glycogen Storage
mechanisms.description: Describes support for the storage of glucose as glycogen in the liver and muscles, an important energy reserve.
mechanisms.plainEnglish: Helps the body store energy as glycogen for later use.

mechanisms.name: Reduces Glycaemic Variability
mechanisms.description: Covers effects that reduce the size and frequency of swings in blood glucose levels over time.
mechanisms.plainEnglish: Helps reduce large swings in blood sugar levels.

mechanisms.name: Supports Synaptic Plasticity
mechanisms.description: Describes support for the brain's ability to form and strengthen connections between neurons, a process underlying learning and adaptation.
mechanisms.plainEnglish: Helps the brain form and strengthen new connections.

mechanisms.name: Supports Cerebral Blood Flow
mechanisms.description: Covers effects that support healthy blood flow to the brain, supplying the oxygen and nutrients needed for normal cognitive function.
mechanisms.plainEnglish: Helps maintain healthy blood flow to the brain.

mechanisms.name: Supports Neuronal Antioxidant Defence
mechanisms.description: Describes antioxidant protection specific to neurons, which are particularly vulnerable to oxidative stress due to their high metabolic activity.
mechanisms.plainEnglish: Helps protect brain cells from oxidative damage.

mechanisms.name: Supports Neurotransmitter Synthesis
mechanisms.description: Covers effects that support the production of neurotransmitters, the chemical messengers that allow neurons to communicate.
mechanisms.plainEnglish: Helps the brain produce the chemical messengers it needs to function.

mechanisms.name: Supports Cognitive Resilience
mechanisms.description: Describes the brain's overall capacity to maintain normal cognitive function under everyday physiological stress and with age.
mechanisms.plainEnglish: Helps support healthy brain function over time.

mechanisms.name: Supports Memory Formation
mechanisms.description: Covers effects on the neurological processes involved in encoding and consolidating new memories.
mechanisms.plainEnglish: Helps support the brain's ability to form new memories.

mechanisms.name: Supports Mental Performance
mechanisms.description: Describes broader effects on attention, focus and cognitive processing speed during everyday mental tasks.
mechanisms.plainEnglish: Helps support focus and mental performance.

mechanisms.name: Supports Nervous System Function
mechanisms.description: A broad mechanism covering general support for healthy signalling and function throughout the nervous system.
mechanisms.plainEnglish: Helps support healthy nervous system function overall.

mechanisms.name: Supports Healthy Mood
mechanisms.description: Covers effects, often via neurotransmitter and inflammatory pathways, associated with supporting normal, healthy mood regulation.
mechanisms.plainEnglish: Helps support healthy mood.

mechanisms.name: Supports Neuroprotection
mechanisms.description: Describes broader protective effects on neurons against oxidative, inflammatory or metabolic stress.
mechanisms.plainEnglish: Helps protect brain cells from everyday stress and damage.

mechanisms.name: Supports Healthy Inflammatory Balance
mechanisms.description: Describes support for a balanced inflammatory response, allowing the body to mount an appropriate response to injury or infection without excessive or prolonged inflammation.
mechanisms.plainEnglish: Helps keep the body's inflammatory response balanced.

mechanisms.name: Supports Innate Immune Function
mechanisms.description: Covers support for the innate immune system, the body's fast-acting, non-specific first line of defence against pathogens.
mechanisms.plainEnglish: Helps support the body's first line of immune defence.

mechanisms.name: Supports Adaptive Immune Function
mechanisms.description: Describes support for the adaptive immune system, which develops targeted, longer-lasting immunity to specific pathogens.
mechanisms.plainEnglish: Helps support the body's targeted, longer-term immune defences.

mechanisms.name: Supports Immune Cell Signalling
mechanisms.description: Covers effects on the communication between immune cells via cytokines and other signalling molecules, important for a coordinated immune response.
mechanisms.plainEnglish: Helps immune cells communicate with each other effectively.

mechanisms.name: Supports Resolution of Inflammation
mechanisms.description: Describes support for the active process by which an inflammatory response is brought to a close once its purpose has been served.
mechanisms.plainEnglish: Helps the body properly wind down inflammation once it's no longer needed.

mechanisms.name: Supports Antimicrobial Defence
mechanisms.description: Covers effects that support the body's natural defences against harmful bacteria and other microbes.
mechanisms.plainEnglish: Helps support the body's natural defences against harmful microbes.

mechanisms.name: Supports Antiviral Defence
mechanisms.description: Describes effects that support the body's natural defences against viral infection.
mechanisms.plainEnglish: Helps support the body's natural defences against viruses.

mechanisms.name: Supports Immune Surveillance
mechanisms.description: Covers the immune system's ongoing monitoring for abnormal or damaged cells and potential threats.
mechanisms.plainEnglish: Helps the immune system keep watch for potential threats.

mechanisms.name: Supports Healthy Cytokine Balance
mechanisms.description: Describes support for a balanced profile of cytokines, the signalling proteins that coordinate immune and inflammatory responses.
mechanisms.plainEnglish: Helps keep the immune system's signalling molecules in balance.

mechanisms.name: Supports Immune Resilience
mechanisms.description: Covers the immune system's overall capacity to respond effectively to everyday challenges while returning to a balanced baseline state.
mechanisms.plainEnglish: Helps support a resilient, well-functioning immune system.

mechanisms.name: Supports Hormone Synthesis
mechanisms.description: Describes support for the biochemical pathways involved in producing hormones from their precursor molecules.
mechanisms.plainEnglish: Helps the body produce the hormones it needs.

mechanisms.name: Supports Thyroid Function
mechanisms.description: Covers support for the thyroid gland's role in producing hormones that regulate metabolism, energy and growth.
mechanisms.plainEnglish: Helps support healthy thyroid function.

mechanisms.name: Supports Insulin Signalling
mechanisms.description: Describes support for the cellular signalling pathways triggered by insulin, which regulate glucose uptake and metabolism.
mechanisms.plainEnglish: Helps the body's cells respond properly to insulin.

mechanisms.name: Supports Sex Hormone Balance
mechanisms.description: Covers effects on the balance of sex hormones such as oestrogen and testosterone, relevant to reproductive and broader physiological health.
mechanisms.plainEnglish: Helps support a healthy balance of sex hormones.
mechanisms.guardrail: This mechanism represents support for normal physiological hormone balance. It is not a claim to treat hormonal disorders or replace hormone therapy.

mechanisms.name: Supports Adrenal Function
mechanisms.description: Describes support for the adrenal glands' role in producing hormones involved in the stress response and metabolism, such as cortisol.
mechanisms.plainEnglish: Helps support healthy adrenal gland function.

mechanisms.name: Supports Oestrogen Metabolism
mechanisms.description: Covers effects on the pathways by which the body's own oestrogen is metabolised and cleared, relevant to healthy hormonal balance.
mechanisms.plainEnglish: Helps support the healthy processing of oestrogen in the body.
mechanisms.guardrail: This mechanism represents support for the body's own oestrogen metabolism and clearance pathways. It is not a claim to treat hormonal conditions or alter hormone levels therapeutically.

mechanisms.name: Supports Testosterone Production
mechanisms.description: Describes support for the physiological pathways involved in producing testosterone.
mechanisms.plainEnglish: Helps support the body's natural testosterone production.
mechanisms.guardrail: This mechanism represents support for normal physiological testosterone production. It is not a claim to treat low testosterone or replace hormone therapy.

mechanisms.name: Supports Hormonal Homeostasis
mechanisms.description: A broad mechanism covering support for the overall balance and regulation of the body's hormonal systems.
mechanisms.plainEnglish: Helps keep the body's hormones in overall balance.

mechanisms.name: Supports Endocrine Resilience
mechanisms.description: Covers the endocrine system's overall capacity to maintain hormonal balance under everyday physiological stress.
mechanisms.plainEnglish: Helps the body's hormone-producing glands stay resilient under stress.

mechanisms.name: Supports Collagen Formation
mechanisms.description: Describes support for collagen synthesis, the primary structural protein in skin, bone, cartilage and connective tissue.
mechanisms.plainEnglish: Helps the body produce collagen, a key structural protein.

mechanisms.name: Supports Bone Mineralisation
mechanisms.description: Covers support for the deposition of calcium and other minerals into bone tissue, contributing to bone density and strength.
mechanisms.plainEnglish: Helps the body build strong, well-mineralised bones.

mechanisms.name: Supports Muscle Protein Synthesis
mechanisms.description: Describes support for the process by which the body builds new muscle protein, important for muscle maintenance, repair and growth.
mechanisms.plainEnglish: Helps the body build and repair muscle tissue.

mechanisms.name: Supports Connective Tissue Integrity
mechanisms.description: Covers support for the structural integrity of tendons, ligaments and other connective tissues throughout the body.
mechanisms.plainEnglish: Helps keep connective tissue, like tendons and ligaments, strong.

mechanisms.name: Supports Joint Health
mechanisms.description: Describes broader support for joint structures and comfort, encompassing cartilage, synovial fluid and surrounding tissue.
mechanisms.plainEnglish: Helps support healthy, comfortable joints.

mechanisms.name: Supports Muscle Recovery
mechanisms.description: Covers effects that support the repair and recovery of muscle tissue following physical activity.
mechanisms.plainEnglish: Helps muscles recover after physical activity.

mechanisms.name: Supports Bone Remodelling
mechanisms.description: Describes support for the ongoing natural process of bone breakdown and rebuilding that maintains skeletal strength throughout life.
mechanisms.plainEnglish: Helps support the body's natural bone renewal process.

mechanisms.name: Supports Tendon Health
mechanisms.description: Covers support for the structure and resilience of tendons, which connect muscle to bone.
mechanisms.plainEnglish: Helps keep tendons strong and resilient.

mechanisms.name: Supports Physical Performance
mechanisms.description: Describes broader effects on strength, endurance or physical capacity during activity.
mechanisms.plainEnglish: Helps support physical performance and stamina.

mechanisms.name: Supports Healthy Ageing of Musculoskeletal System
mechanisms.description: Covers the combined effects that support bone, muscle and joint health as part of healthy ageing.
mechanisms.plainEnglish: Helps support strong bones, muscles and joints as part of healthy ageing.

mechanisms.name: Supports Neurotrophic Signalling
mechanisms.description: Supports neurotrophic signalling pathways involved in neuronal maintenance, adaptation and plasticity.
mechanisms.plainEnglish: Helps support the growth signals that keep brain cells healthy and adaptable.

mechanisms.name: Supports Blood-Brain Barrier Integrity
mechanisms.description: Supports the integrity and protective function of the blood-brain barrier, helping maintain controlled exchange between the circulation and nervous tissue.
mechanisms.plainEnglish: Helps protect the barrier that shields the brain from harmful substances in the blood.

mechanisms.name: Supports Cellular Energy Metabolism
mechanisms.description: Supports cellular processes involved in energy production and utilisation, including mitochondrial activity and ATP generation. This is a cross-system mechanism that may apply to multiple body systems where evidence supports a role for cellular energy metabolism.
mechanisms.plainEnglish: Helps cells produce and use energy efficiently.

mechanisms.name: Supports Healthy Airway Inflammatory Balance
mechanisms.description: Supports healthy regulation of inflammatory activity within the airways and respiratory tissues.
mechanisms.plainEnglish: Helps keep inflammation in the airways balanced.

mechanisms.name: Supports Healthy Airway Reactivity
mechanisms.description: Supports healthy regulation of airway responsiveness, including physiological control of bronchial reactivity.
mechanisms.plainEnglish: Helps keep the airways responding normally rather than overreacting.

mechanisms.name: Supports Airway Barrier Integrity
mechanisms.description: Supports the integrity and protective function of the respiratory epithelial barrier.
mechanisms.plainEnglish: Helps protect the lining of the airways.

mechanisms.name: Supports Renal Cellular Protection
mechanisms.description: Supports protection of renal cells and tissues against cellular stress, including oxidative, inflammatory and metabolic stress.
mechanisms.plainEnglish: Helps protect kidney cells from everyday stress and damage.

mechanisms.name: Supports Menopausal Transition Resilience
mechanisms.description: Supports physiological resilience and adaptation during the hormonal transition associated with perimenopause and menopause.
mechanisms.plainEnglish: Supports physiological adaptation during the menopausal transition.
mechanisms.guardrail: This mechanism represents physiological adaptation during the menopausal transition. It is not a claim to treat menopause, replace hormone therapy, or normalise hormone concentrations.

mechanisms.name: Supports Phytoestrogen Metabolism
mechanisms.description: Supports microbial and host processing of dietary phytoestrogens into bioactive metabolites and influences their bioavailability and biological activity.
mechanisms.plainEnglish: Supports the gut-mediated processing of plant compounds with oestrogen-like activity.
mechanisms.guardrail: This mechanism represents metabolism and bioavailability of dietary phytoestrogens. It is not a claim that phytoestrogens replace endogenous oestrogen, treat menopause, or normalise hormone concentrations.

mechanisms.name: Supports Phase I Detoxification
mechanisms.description: Supports hepatic Phase I biotransformation of endogenous compounds and xenobiotics through cytochrome P450 enzyme activity.
mechanisms.plainEnglish: Helps the liver begin breaking down toxins and unwanted compounds.

mechanisms.name: Supports Phase II Conjugation
mechanisms.description: Supports conjugation pathways including glutathione, glucuronidation and sulfation that prepare compounds for safe elimination.
mechanisms.plainEnglish: Helps the liver make toxins water-soluble so they can be removed safely.

mechanisms.name: Supports Glutathione Synthesis
mechanisms.description: Supports endogenous production and recycling of glutathione, the body's principal intracellular antioxidant and detoxification molecule.
mechanisms.plainEnglish: Helps the body produce and recycle glutathione, its main natural detox molecule.

mechanisms.name: Supports Xenobiotic Elimination
mechanisms.description: Supports the transport and elimination of metabolised environmental compounds, pollutants and metabolic waste.
mechanisms.plainEnglish: Helps the body remove processed toxins and waste products.

mechanisms.name: Supports Hepatic Cellular Protection
mechanisms.description: Supports resilience and protection of liver cells during normal metabolic and detoxification activity.
mechanisms.plainEnglish: Helps protect liver cells while the liver performs detoxification.
